title: Emanuel Ax, piano & Yo-Yo Ma, cello
description:
To be in the room when Yo-Yo Ma and Emanuel Ax perform together is to witness a musical relationship shaped by more than four decades of friendship, trust, and curiosity. Ax has described their collaboration as one in which the music leads and the musicians follow. Their performances carry an ease and intimacy that only comes from years of listening closely to one another, responding in the moment, and returning again and again to the joy of making music together.

 

What makes this collaboration remarkable is not simply technical mastery. It is the sense of connection that runs through every note. Audiences can hear it in the way one musician follows the other’s lead, anticipates a phrase, or finds space for an unexpected idea to emerge.

 

Both artists are familiar faces at Carolina Performing Arts; Ma through multiple appearances with the Silkroad Ensemble and Ax through recitals and orchestral performances. Experiencing them together offers a rare opportunity to witness two lifelong friends in conversation through music.

 

Student tickets always $11. Eligible for CLE. Find out more and buy tickets at: https://carolinaperformingarts.org/events/emanuelax-yoyoma/

title: STREB EXTREME ACTION DO NOT TRY THIS AT HOME
description:
What can the human body do? Or maybe, what can it not do?

 

In DO NOT TRY THIS AT HOME, STREB performers—called “Action Heroes”—dive, fling, flip, and fall off of massive moving structures with split-second timing and fearless precision. Audiences gasp, laugh, tense up, and wonder how what they’re seeing is even possible.

 

Founder Elizabeth Streb has been called the Evel Knievel of dance, a thrill-seeker, and a Superwoman. She is the founder of SLAM—the STREB Lab for Action Mechanics—in Brooklyn, where her company has spent decades developing a movement practice called PopAction: a fusion acrobatics, rodeo, dance and athletics, rooted in a lifelong obsession with what happens to the human body when it is fully, fearlessly committed to motion. Her philosophy: “Anything too safe is not action.”

 

The company transforms physical risk into spectacles of wonder, exploring the outer extremes of human movement, asking what becomes possible when courage, creativity, athleticism, and engineering collide.

 

Student tickets always $11. Eligible for CLE. Find out more and buy tickets at: https://carolinaperformingarts.org/events/streb/

title: Hidden Battleship Tour
description:
Offered only four times this coming year, Hidden Battleship takes adventurous visitors beyond the traditional self-guided tour and into unrestored areas of the Battleship North Carolina Memorial that are normally closed to the public. Led by experienced guides in small groups, participants explore spaces deep below deck, throughout the third deck, in the bow, and high into the Ship's superstructure—including all the way to the top.

The 2027 Hidden Battleship tours will be offered on:

Saturday, February 27Saturday, March 20Saturday, April 24Saturday, November 20Each tour runs from 11:00 am to 5:00 pm. The cost is $75 per participant, plus tax.

Designed for adventurous history enthusiasts, the six-hour experience requires climbing ladders, crossing high hatches, and navigating tight and confined spaces. For that reason, the program is limited to participants ages 16 and older.

"Every compartment aboard the Battleship has a story," said Dr. Jay Martin, Executive Director of Battleship North Carolina Memorial. "Hidden Battleship opens doors that are normally closed, inviting visitors to step into the spaces where sailors lived, worked, and fought—and to experience the Ship in a way very few people ever will."

Because attendance is intentionally limited to provide a safe, behind-the-scenes experience, Hidden Battleship consistently sells out well in advance. The experience has become a favorite among repeat visitors, military history enthusiasts, photographers, and anyone looking to explore a side of the Ship that few ever have the opportunity to see.

Whether you're searching for a memorable gift or your next great adventure, Hidden Battleship offers an unforgettable behind-the-scenes experience unlike any other.

Visitors are encouraged to reserve their spots early. Tickets and additional information are available at https://bit.ly/hiddenbattleship

title: Forging A Nation: North Carolina in the America Revolution Exhibit
description: This exhibit explores how North Carolina helped forge a new nation during one of the most transformative periods in history. Through maps, historical documents, and everyday objects, this exhibit reveals the state’s role in the struggle for independence, from early protests against British rule and the battles fought on Carolina soil to the drafting of the Constitution. Forging a Nation invites visitors to witness how ordinary people, conflict, and conviction shaped North Carolina's history during the American Revolution.

title: Mecklenburg's Declaration: NC's Revolutionary Presbyterians
description:
An article published in the April 30, 1819 edition of the Raleigh Register and North Carolina Gazette proclaimed the following: “It is not probably known to many of our readers, that the citizens of Mecklenburg County, in this State, made a Declaration of Independence more than a year before Congress made theirs. The following Document on the subject has lately come to the hands of the Editor from unquestionable authority,  and is published that it may go down to posterity.”  

The document in question was called the Mecklenburg Declaration of Independence, and it had allegedly declared Mecklenburg “free and independent” from British rule on May 20, 1775. Of the 27 men who were said to have signed the document, almost all were Presbyterian.

But many people were confused – why were they just now hearing about this revolutionary action? The original document burned in a house fire in 1800, and the published version had been reconstructed from notes made by the clerk of the 1775 meeting. No extant copies could be found.

The debate over the authenticity of the Mecklenburg Declaration began. And, when a copy of a document called the Mecklenburg Resolves written on May 30, 1775, was discovered in a 1775 newspaper, the debate intensified. The Resolves were revolutionary, but stopped short of declaring independence. Did both documents exist? Or was the Declaration being conflated with the Resolves?

Examine the evidence and decide for yourself by visiting the new exhibit, “Mecklenburg Declaration?” at the Presbyterian Heritage Center.

The PHC is open Tuesday-Friday (10-4) and Saturday (12-4).

title: “To BEethoven Rather Than To Seem”: Part V | Gut Instinct Chamber Music Project
description:
FEATURING

Nicholas DiEguenio, violin
Mimi Solomon, piano

 

PROGRAM

Featuring Beethoven’s “Spring” Sonata and Robert Honstein’s Olmsted

This season, Gut Instinct takes on the large-scale project “To Beethoven Rather Than To Seem,” marking 200 years since Beethoven’s death and 250 since the U.S. Declaration of Independence. Over the course of five concerts, Nicholas DiEugenio and pianist Mimi Solomon will present all ten Beethoven Sonatas on period instruments along with five commissioned works written expressly for them.

 

PARKING

Please plan to arrive early as parking on campus can be tricky. Learn more about parking and directions to UNC-Chapel Hill’s campus.

 

The Gut Instinct Chamber Music Project, now in its third season, is a concert series in the Triangle area which brings UNC-Chapel Hill and Duke University’s historical instrument collections together with artists committed to presenting inspired, visceral, historically informed performances of the 19th-century chamber music repertoire. The series features music of female composers and their artistic circles. The name “Gut Instinct” is a play on words. In 19th-century Europe, the violin, viola, and cello were strung with (sheep) gut.

 

All of the artists collaborating with the Pleyel and Graf pianos at UNC-Chapel Hill (built in 19th-century Paris and Vienna, respectively), as well as the Clementi piano at Duke (early 19th-century England) use these gut string materials. The turn of phrase “gut instinct” also refers to the visceral, accessible nature of the musical performances that this series presents. Our mission is to make “Historically Informed Performance” accessible, relatable, and culturally relevant! We also want to feature these special pianos that are rarely heard by the public, along with great music by female composers which has remained lesser known to the greater public for far too long, and living composers who are keeping our art form alive!

title: Nature Tales Story Time
location: North Carolina Botanical Garden, 100 Old Mason Farm Road, Chapel Hill, NC, 27517, United States
description:
Bring your little one for a morning or afternoon of stories, songs, and outdoor discovery! Nature Tales is a monthly family program for children ages 3-7 and a grown-up, where a nature-themed story comes to life through hands-on exploration in the garden.
 Who? Children ages 3-7, with an adult When? 10 a.m. to 11 a.m. or 3:30 p.m. to 4:30 p.m. Where? North Carolina Botanical Garden Cost? $5 per child (free for members and families receiving SNAP benefits) 
Know a family who’d love this? Share the event!  
Upcoming Dates: 
Friday, December 11th – Where Did Everyone Go? 
Where do animals go when winter arrives? Some migrate, some hibernate, some stay busy all winter, and some find cozy places to hide. After the story, head outside to look for clues that animals are still around, even when we don’t see them! The program will happen rain or shine, with indoor activities if the weather is unfavorable. Register here for morning session or afternoon session. 
More dates to come! Check back soon.

title: Downtown Techies Durham and Raleigh MERGE FOR THE SUMMER!
description:
Downtown Techies: Durham
Hey Techies!

We are so excited to see you all again! Heads up! for the summer months we are merging all of our events into an event once a month on the first Tuesday of every month!

Don't forget to RSVP for first round free!!

We will be resuming Downtown Durham events in September on the third Tuesday of every month. We would love your suggestions on venues! Just ping us.

Questions or suggestions?

Our digital door is always open at www.downtowntechies.com or @downtowntechies. Check out our events in Raleigh as well!

Meet, Drink and be TECHIE!

description: This exhibit explores how North Carolina helped forge a new nation during one of the most transformative periods in history. Through maps, historical documents, and everyday objects, this exhibit reveals the state’s role in the struggle for independence, from early protests against British rule and the battles fought on Carolina soil to the drafting of the Constitution. Forging a Nation invites visitors to witness how ordinary people, conflict, and conviction shaped North Carolina's history during the American Revolution.

title: Educators of Excellence Yellowstone Summer Institute
location: Yellowstone National Park, Montana and Wyoming and Raleigh, N.C.
description:
Applications for Summer 2027 Yellowstone Institute is now open.

Experience one of North America’s greatest concentrations of wildlife.Observe world-class geological wonders.Learn about the history and management of America’s first national park.Learn from scientists and experts.Participating educators will study and experience the wonders of our first national park. Join us from sunrise to sunset as we observe the incredible wildlife of Yellowstone, including bears, bison, wolves and elk. Learn about the area’s unique geology while exploring the amazing world of geysers, hot springs and mudpots. Enjoy the magnificent scenery of the northern Rocky Mountains as we hike trails throughout the park. The daily program will include field experiences, opportunities to meet with park staff and other experts, and activities designed to help integrate your experiences into the classroom. Discover strategies for exploring the connections between Yellowstone and North Carolina — wolf and elk reintroduction, fire ecology, resource management issues and much more. Students can follow along and ask questions as we post daily blogs from the field.

Dates: June 14-22, 2027 (Mandatory pre- and post-trip sessions will be held in Raleigh on Saturday, April 3, 2027 and Saturday, November 6, 2027.)

Locations: Yellowstone National Park, Montana and Wyoming and Raleigh, N.C.

Group Size: Limited to 12 participants.

Activity Level: Moderate to rigorous including walking and hiking (up to 5 miles) on uneven terrain at high altitudes.

Cost: $1600*
Includes round-trip airfare from Raleigh to Bozeman, MT; all ground transportation; instruction and lodging. Participants will be responsible for travel to and from Raleigh, expenses in Raleigh during pre- and post-trip sessions, and most meals in Yellowstone. See below for scholarship opportunities.

*The cost of all Institutes are significantly reduced thanks the generous support of the Friends of the Museum, Goodnight Educational Foundation, and the Gibson Family Foundation. Teachers that apply and are selected from the list of eastern counties (see below for details) may be eligible to receive a Simple Gifts Scholarship, which is provided through the generous support of the Simple Gifts Fund and the Anonymous Trust. 

Apply now by Friday, February 19, 2027!
 

REQUIREMENTS AND APPLICATIONS

Who’s Eligible: Classroom teachers of all subject areas, school administrators, informal educators and university professors who work with teachers.

Qualifications: All applicants must currently be working as full-time educators in North Carolina and must expect to continue working in or with North Carolina schools during the following school year. Applicants must have at least three years of teaching/supervising experience. Applicants should demonstrate an interest in the natural sciences and be willing to use and support innovative teaching methods in the classroom and on field trips. All participants should be prepared for moderately strenuous activity.

Requirements: Participants must attend all portion of the program, including the mandatory pre- and post-trip meetings at the Museum in Raleigh. After the trip, participants must develop an educational project incorporating their experience from the Institute. Projects will be presented at the post-trip meeting in November. Participants are encouraged to share their projects at meetings or conferences of professional organizations.

Selection: The Museum strives to achieve statewide representation from diverse backgrounds and a range of grade levels. Preference is given to educators who show evidence of institutional support, flexibility and a tendency to be active group participants.

Credit: Institutes may be approved for renewal credits by local school districts. Participants receive a certificate of course completion for the number of instructional hours. Participants can also receive credit for the NC Environmental Education Certification Program (more information at www.eenorthcarolina.org).

Financial Support: The cost of all Educators of Excellence Institutes is reduced thanks to generous support from the Goodnight Educational Foundation and Gibson Family Foundation through the Educators of Excellence Fund. Participant fees reflect about one third of the total cost of the Institute.

***We do not want cost to be a barrier for any educator. Many participants receive financial support from their schools and/or local civic or professional organizations; contact your local district office for information on grants and scholarships. If the cost of the Institute would prevent your participation, you are unable to obtain funding from an alternative funding source, and you do not qualify for the Simple Gifts Scholarship, please reach out to Megan Davis.

The Simple Gifts Scholarship is provided through the generous support of the Simple Gifts Fund and the Anonymous Trust, which strives to enrich and improve the lives of motivated, rural Eastern NC teachers and their students. The Simple Gifts Scholarship seeks to support teachers who recognize the value of inquiry, who understand the power of knowledge and who appreciate the importance of inspiring excellence in their students. Applicants who are chosen to participate in the one of the 2027 Educators of Excellence Institutes and meet the following criteria will be eligible for a full scholarship covering the cost of the experience. Once selected, applicants will be responsible for paying a $200 deposit that will be returned to them upon successful completion of the program.

To be considered for the Simple Gifts Scholarship, applicants must:

Have not previously received the Simple Gifts Scholarship for an Educators of Excellence Institute.Be a teacher, guidance counselor, media coordinator or assistant principal in a public school, in one of the following counties:
Beaufort, Bertie, Bladen, Chowan, Columbus, Craven, Cumberland, Duplin, Edgecombe, Gates, Greene, Halifax, Hertford, Hyde, Jones, Lenoir, Martin, Nash, Northampton, Onslow, Pamlico, Pasquotank, Perquimans, Pitt, Robeson, Sampson, Scotland, Tyrrell, Washington, Wayne, WilsonPlan to continue working in their current school system and county during the following school year.Plan to continue working full time as an educator in a North Carolina county from the above list for at least 5 more years after participation in the Institute.Help spread the word about future Educators of Excellence Institutes and the Simple Gifts Scholarship to other teachersNOT be teaching in NC while on an J-1 or H-1B visa. We regret that our international exchange teachers are not eligible for this particular scholarship.All applications received by the deadline will be considered equally, so please do not rush your application! The selection process for this program is competitive, so please make sure you take your time and fully complete the application. All applicants must have a complete Educator Application and a Supervisor Application. 

Educator Application 

Supervisor Application

title: Educators of Excellence Yellowstone Summer Institute
location: Yellowstone National Park, Montana and Wyoming and Raleigh, N.C.
description:
Applications for Summer 2027 Yellowstone Institute is now open.

Experience one of North America’s greatest concentrations of wildlife.Observe world-class geological wonders.Learn about the history and management of America’s first national park.Learn from scientists and experts.Participating educators will study and experience the wonders of our first national park. Join us from sunrise to sunset as we observe the incredible wildlife of Yellowstone, including bears, bison, wolves and elk. Learn about the area’s unique geology while exploring the amazing world of geysers, hot springs and mudpots. Enjoy the magnificent scenery of the northern Rocky Mountains as we hike trails throughout the park. The daily program will include field experiences, opportunities to meet with park staff and other experts, and activities designed to help integrate your experiences into the classroom. Discover strategies for exploring the connections between Yellowstone and North Carolina — wolf and elk reintroduction, fire ecology, resource management issues and much more. Students can follow along and ask questions as we post daily blogs from the field.

Dates: June 14-22, 2027 (Mandatory pre- and post-trip sessions will be held in Raleigh on Saturday, April 3, 2027 and Saturday, November 6, 2027.)

Locations: Yellowstone National Park, Montana and Wyoming and Raleigh, N.C.

Group Size: Limited to 12 participants.

Activity Level: Moderate to rigorous including walking and hiking (up to 5 miles) on uneven terrain at high altitudes.

Cost: $1600*
Includes round-trip airfare from Raleigh to Bozeman, MT; all ground transportation; instruction and lodging. Participants will be responsible for travel to and from Raleigh, expenses in Raleigh during pre- and post-trip sessions, and most meals in Yellowstone. See below for scholarship opportunities.

*The cost of all Institutes are significantly reduced thanks the generous support of the Friends of the Museum, Goodnight Educational Foundation, and the Gibson Family Foundation. Teachers that apply and are selected from the list of eastern counties (see below for details) may be eligible to receive a Simple Gifts Scholarship, which is provided through the generous support of the Simple Gifts Fund and the Anonymous Trust. 

Apply now by Friday, February 19, 2027!
 

REQUIREMENTS AND APPLICATIONS

Who’s Eligible: Classroom teachers of all subject areas, school administrators, informal educators and university professors who work with teachers.

Qualifications: All applicants must currently be working as full-time educators in North Carolina and must expect to continue working in or with North Carolina schools during the following school year. Applicants must have at least three years of teaching/supervising experience. Applicants should demonstrate an interest in the natural sciences and be willing to use and support innovative teaching methods in the classroom and on field trips. All participants should be prepared for moderately strenuous activity.

Requirements: Participants must attend all portion of the program, including the mandatory pre- and post-trip meetings at the Museum in Raleigh. After the trip, participants must develop an educational project incorporating their experience from the Institute. Projects will be presented at the post-trip meeting in November. Participants are encouraged to share their projects at meetings or conferences of professional organizations.

Selection: The Museum strives to achieve statewide representation from diverse backgrounds and a range of grade levels. Preference is given to educators who show evidence of institutional support, flexibility and a tendency to be active group participants.

Credit: Institutes may be approved for renewal credits by local school districts. Participants receive a certificate of course completion for the number of instructional hours. Participants can also receive credit for the NC Environmental Education Certification Program (more information at www.eenorthcarolina.org).

Financial Support: The cost of all Educators of Excellence Institutes is reduced thanks to generous support from the Goodnight Educational Foundation and Gibson Family Foundation through the Educators of Excellence Fund. Participant fees reflect about one third of the total cost of the Institute.

***We do not want cost to be a barrier for any educator. Many participants receive financial support from their schools and/or local civic or professional organizations; contact your local district office for information on grants and scholarships. If the cost of the Institute would prevent your participation, you are unable to obtain funding from an alternative funding source, and you do not qualify for the Simple Gifts Scholarship, please reach out to Megan Davis.

The Simple Gifts Scholarship is provided through the generous support of the Simple Gifts Fund and the Anonymous Trust, which strives to enrich and improve the lives of motivated, rural Eastern NC teachers and their students. The Simple Gifts Scholarship seeks to support teachers who recognize the value of inquiry, who understand the power of knowledge and who appreciate the importance of inspiring excellence in their students. Applicants who are chosen to participate in the one of the 2027 Educators of Excellence Institutes and meet the following criteria will be eligible for a full scholarship covering the cost of the experience. Once selected, applicants will be responsible for paying a $200 deposit that will be returned to them upon successful completion of the program.

To be considered for the Simple Gifts Scholarship, applicants must:

Have not previously received the Simple Gifts Scholarship for an Educators of Excellence Institute.Be a teacher, guidance counselor, media coordinator or assistant principal in a public school, in one of the following counties:
Beaufort, Bertie, Bladen, Chowan, Columbus, Craven, Cumberland, Duplin, Edgecombe, Gates, Greene, Halifax, Hertford, Hyde, Jones, Lenoir, Martin, Nash, Northampton, Onslow, Pamlico, Pasquotank, Perquimans, Pitt, Robeson, Sampson, Scotland, Tyrrell, Washington, Wayne, WilsonPlan to continue working in their current school system and county during the following school year.Plan to continue working full time as an educator in a North Carolina county from the above list for at least 5 more years after participation in the Institute.Help spread the word about future Educators of Excellence Institutes and the Simple Gifts Scholarship to other teachersNOT be teaching in NC while on an J-1 or H-1B visa. We regret that our international exchange teachers are not eligible for this particular scholarship.All applications received by the deadline will be considered equally, so please do not rush your application! The selection process for this program is competitive, so please make sure you take your time and fully complete the application. All applicants must have a complete Educator Application and a Supervisor Application. 

Educator Application 

Supervisor Application

title: Battle of Ramsour's Mill
description:
The Battle of Ramsour’s Mill Living History Weekend commemorates the June 20, 1780 Battle of Ramsour’s Mill, when Whigs met Tories on a hillside just outside the little town of Lincolnton.

In 2026, the commemoration will take place the weekend of June 20 & 21 near Battleground Elementary School.

In between, hearth cooking demonstrations by the Lincoln County Hearth Cooks, reenactments and weapons demonstrations, a militia encampment, speakers and storytellers, heritage demonstrations, battleground tours, and period crafts. All activities are free.

Schedule is subject to change. Reenactors and demonstrators welcome! Reenactors who wish to participate should contact Lisa Pupkiewicz at lpupkie@gmail.com; suttlers should contact Beverly Moore at bkingnccp@gmail.com

title: People of Colonial North Carolina Exhibit
description: Explore the diverse stories of those who called North Carolina home during the American Revolution in this compelling traveling exhibit. People of Colonial North Carolina highlights the complex and often conflicting paths different communities took in the fight for freedom and survival. Through maps, rare documents, and illustrations, the exhibit offers a look at how the American Revolution impacted everyday lives.

title: NC Public Librarian Certification Commission
description:
The NC Public Librarian Certification Commission was formed in 1936 to set minimum standards for public librarians to protect and maintain public library resources, to assure professional management and administration of library services, to meet the personnel requirements for State Aid administered by the Library of NC, and to guarantee the best possible public library service to all North Carolinians.

The North Carolina General Statute 143B-68 states that the commission must be comprised of: the Chairman of the public libraries section of NCLA, two individuals named by the Governor upon nomination of the NCLA, the dean of a State or regionally accredited graduate school of librarianship in North Carolina appointed by the Governor, and one member at large appointed by the Governor. Commission members appointed by the Governor serve 4-year terms, all others serve 2-year terms.

Commission meetings are held quarterly to review applications and discuss Certification policies and procedures.

The commission's meeting dates for the 2025-2026 year are October 27, 2025, January 9, 2026, April 10, 2026, and July 10, 2026. All meetings are held at the Library of NC beginning at 1:00 pm unless otherwise posted. Information about meetings can be found on the North Carolina Secretary of State's meeting calendar.

Have questions about certification? Contact us at NC.Certification.Commission@dncr.nc.gov.

Locations: Multiple sites in western North Carolina and Raleigh, NC.

Group Size: Limited to 10 participants.

Activity Level: Moderate to rigorous activity including camping most nights, walking and hiking on uneven terrain (up to 5 miles), and swimming and snorkeling in cold mountain streams.

Cost: $800*
Includes campsites and lodging, all meals, instruction, and supporting materials. The Museum can lend most camping gear if you do not have your own. Participants will be responsible for travel to and from Raleigh, expenses in Raleigh during pre- and post-trip sessions. See below for scholarship opportunities.

*The cost of all Institutes are significantly reduced thanks the generous support of the Friends of the Museum, the Goodnight Educational Foundation, and the Gibson Family Foundation. Apply now by Friday, February 19, 2027!
 

REQUIREMENTS AND APPLICATIONS

Who’s Eligible: Classroom teachers of all subject areas, school administrators, informal educators and university professors who work with teachers.

Qualifications: All applicants must currently be working as full-time educators in North Carolina and must expect to continue working in or with North Carolina schools during the following school year. Applicants must have at least three years of teaching/supervising experience. Applicants should demonstrate an interest in the natural sciences and be willing to use and support innovative teaching methods in the classroom and on field trips. All participants should be prepared for moderately strenuous activity.

Requirements: Participants must attend all portion of the program, including the mandatory pre- and post-trip meetings at the Museum in Raleigh. After the trip, participants must develop an educational project incorporating their experience from the Institute. Projects will be presented at the post-trip meeting in November. Participants are encouraged to share their projects at meetings or conferences of professional organizations.

Selection: The Museum strives to achieve statewide representation from diverse backgrounds and a range of grade levels. Preference is given to educators who show evidence of institutional support, flexibility and a tendency to be active group participants.

Credit: Institutes may be approved for renewal credits by local school districts. Participants receive a certificate of course completion for the number of instructional hours. Participants can also receive credit for the NC Environmental Education Certification Program (more information at www.eenorthcarolina.org).

Financial Support: The cost of all Educators of Excellence Institutes is reduced thanks to generous support from the Goodnight Educational Foundation and Gibson Family Foundation through the Educators of Excellence Fund. Participant fees reflect about one third of the total cost of the Institute.

***We do not want cost to be a barrier for any educator. Many participants receive financial support from their schools and/or local civic or professional organizations; contact your local district office for information on grants and scholarships. If the cost of the Institute would prevent your participation, you are unable to obtain funding from an alternative funding source, and you do not qualify for the Simple Gifts Scholarship, please reach out to Megan Davis.

The Simple Gifts Scholarship is provided through the generous support of the Simple Gifts Fund and the Anonymous Trust, which strives to enrich and improve the lives of motivated, rural Eastern NC teachers and their students. The Simple Gifts Scholarship seeks to support teachers who recognize the value of inquiry, who understand the power of knowledge and who appreciate the importance of inspiring excellence in their students. Applicants who are chosen to participate in the one of the 2027 Educators of Excellence Institutes and meet the following criteria will be eligible for a full scholarship covering the cost of the experience. Once selected, applicants will be responsible for paying a $200 deposit that will be returned to them upon successful completion of the program.

To be considered for the Simple Gifts Scholarship, applicants must:

Have not previously received the Simple Gifts Scholarship for an Educators of Excellence Institute.Be a teacher, guidance counselor, media coordinator or assistant principal in a public school, in one of the following counties:
Beaufort, Bertie, Bladen, Chowan, Columbus, Craven, Cumberland, Duplin, Edgecombe, Gates, Greene, Halifax, Hertford, Hyde, Jones, Lenoir, Martin, Nash, Northampton, Onslow, Pamlico, Pasquotank, Perquimans, Pitt, Robeson, Sampson, Scotland, Tyrrell, Washington, Wayne, WilsonPlan to continue working in their current school system and county during the following school year.Plan to continue working full time as an educator in a North Carolina county from the above list for at least 5 more years after participation in the Institute.Help spread the word about future Educators of Excellence Institutes and the Simple Gifts Scholarship to other teachersNOT be teaching in NC while on an J-1 or H-1B visa. We regret that our international exchange teachers are not eligible for this particular scholarship.All applications received by the deadline will be considered equally, so please do not rush your application! The selection process for this program is competitive, so please make sure you take your time and fully complete the application. All applicants must have a complete Educator Application and a Supervisor Application. 

Educator Application

title: Fall Foliage 2027: Lake Placid, NY & The Adirondacks
description:
Triangle Hiking and Outdoors Group
Join THOG for another epic trip to Lake Placid, NY and the Adirondack Mountains. Instead of a solar eclipse, the main event will be the spectacular Fall Colors in northern New York. Other highlights of this trip include the Fall activities in and near Lake Placid, Whiteface Mountain and the surrounding region as well the hikes on the summit trails in The Adirondacks.

PLEASE read this event description carefully

Our overnight accommodations in Lake Placid will be at one of the newest hotels. Note: Hotel availability is limited due to the popularity of this area in the fall.

This will be another two-day road trip event with a hotel stay at around the half-way mark. There will be an option to fly in as well.

**RSVP’s are now open! RSVP Instructions below!**
Trip will be from September 22, 2027- September 28, 2027
Hotel stay in Allentown, PA on the night of 09/22/27 and 09/27/27
Lake Placid stay will be (4 Nights) from 09/23/27-09/26/27 (Thursday-Monday morning)
-Add yourself to the waiting list
-You will be sent the hotel information for Lake Placid, NY and Allentown, PA through Meetup Messages
-Make your reservations or contact and team up with someone on the waiting list to share a room with first to reduce costs then reserve room
-Once your reservations are confirmed, you will be added to the "Going" list
-Each THOG member will be allowed one guest as their plus one.

Our trip begins on Wednesday, September 22, 2027 from the Triangle with an overnight stop in Allentown, PA. On day two, we will stop at a waterfall along the way, as we make our way to Lake Placid. We’ll then spend four amazing days in the Lake Placid/Adirondack Mtn region. We depart Lake Placid on September 27 to head to Allentown. The next morning we leave and arrive in the Triangle that evening. Our drive up and down the US will include strategic stops along the way to make the road trip enjoyable.
Our itinerary will include:
\- Summit hikes and other hikes in the Adirondacks to do some leaf peeping which may include Whiteface Mountain\, Owl Head Overlook\, Coney Mountain\, OK Slip Falls\, High Falls Gorge\, Azure Mountain\, and others\. In addition\, we’ll visit some waterfalls\.
\- Oktoberfest celebration on Whiteface Mountain as well as hike to the Whiteface Mountain summit which has amazing views at over 4\,800ft\.
\- Great Adirondack Moose Festival at Indian Lake\, NY if it's that weekend\,
-Exploring Lake Placid Fall events and downtown
-Visiting Olympic Village, the Olympic Museum and ice skating in Olympic Center.
We will have a more detailed itinerary as the trip gets closer. Please stay together as a group during this event. If you are wanting to do other things separate from the group, this trip may not be for you.

TRAVEL COSTS associated with this event include hotel for a total of 6 nights and gas sharing costs, which are estimated to be around $1,300 but can be reduced if you share hotel rooms. This doesn’t include the costs of food and drinks, admission to the venues, or souvenirs.

Once we know how many people will be going on this trip, we'll form carpools. We will need enough drivers for the trip up to Lake Placid and back. I'll be planning this trip in such a way that it will be as comfortable, accommodating and fun as possible.
If you decide to fly, let me know first before making your reservation.

IMPORTANT: We will have an in-person meeting for those going on this trip. It will take place sometime in March 2027 to discuss some trip logistics and updates to the itinerary. Please plan to attend.

By participating in this event, you agree to the terms below:

TRIP PARTICIPANT WAIVER OF LIABILITY I fully realize that this activity involves a risk of personal injury, property damage, or loss of my person or property. I hereby for myself, my heirs, executors and administrators, and same for persons with whom are in my party, waive and release any claims or rights against Triangle Hiking & Outdoors Group (THOG), all of its owners and coordinators for any and all injury, damages or loss to my person or property incurred during this activity. I also understand that THOG organizers are not required, nor should it be assumed that they are CPR/First Aid/Wilderness Survival Certified and I am responsible for my own personal safety.
Questions about this event?
Please comment below or send me a Meetup message.
-Larredo

title: Building an AI powered, global scale messaging system with XMPP &Deep Learning
description:
Triangle AI Meetup
This talk is an in-depth look at XMPP, the open standard for real-time messaging, and how to build a global scale, AI enhanced messaging system using XMPP. We’ll explore EJabberD, the massively scalable, open-source XMPP server that powers in-game chat for Eve Online, and examine how to: combine XMPP with WebRTC for real-time audio/video calling, add AIML to build helpful chatbots, and how to incorporate Deep Learning to categorize messages in real-time. After the talk, you’ll know how to use XMPP and Ejabberd to build anything from a help-desk chatops application, to a globe spanning in-game messaging system.
